output.text:
## Transcription

**Header label:** BILLING DOCUMENT
**Header (right):** Alder & Finch Repairs — Remedial Works Invoice

**Title:** Invoice
**Company:** Alder & Finch Repairs

**Invoice reference:** NBL-019-INV-11
**Invoice date:** 11 September 2025
**Property:** 18 Brindle Row, Larkspur Vale, ZZ1 1ZZ

**Work invoiced**
- Replaced the broken lounge floorboard and reinstated carpet.
- Removed the front lounge blind and supplied and installed a new Venetian blind.
- Refixed the cupboard handle with new fixings.
- Adjusted the kitchen blind mechanism.
- Retightened the toilet seat.
- Reattached the front-gate hinge with new fixings.

| Description | Amount |
|---|---|
| Remedial works | £174.00 |

The page has no other text, and the footer area is blank apart from a divider line.

## Unclear, missing or inconsistent

- **Single lump-sum charge:** the £174.00 is not itemised. It does not break down labour, materials (floorboard, carpet, Venetian blind, fixings) or cost per task.
- **No VAT information:** it does not say whether the amount includes or excludes VAT, and there is no VAT number, subtotal or total line.
- **No payer or client details:** there is no "bill to" name or address, and no landlord, tenant or agent is identified.
- **Supplier details missing:** there is no address, contact details, company or VAT registration number, or bank/payment details.
- **No payment terms or due date.**
- **No work dates:** only the invoice date is given, not when the work was carried out.
- **No quantities, hours or rates.**
- **Location of some items unspecified:** the cupboard handle and toilet seat have no room named. The "front-gate hinge" is external, and the document does not link any of the items to a job or work order other than the reference NBL-019-INV-11, which may relate to a wider job number but is not explained.
- **Possible scope question:** replacing the front lounge blind with a new Venetian blind is a supply-and-install item, and it is not stated whether it was authorised or why it was replaced rather than repaired.
- **Cost plausibility:** a single £174.00 charge covering a floorboard replacement, carpet reinstatement, a new blind and four minor repairs may warrant checking against a quote, but the document itself gives no basis for comparison.

Hi Rowan,

Thank you for invoice NBL-019-INV-11 (£174.00) for 18 Brindle Row, Larkspur Vale, ZZ1 1ZZ (our ref R/019). Our instruction of 7 September asked for a quotation only, so we can't process the invoice until we have the following:

1. The date and time you attended, and how you got into the property. It is vacant, and the keys were held by our office.
2. Before and after photos of each of the six items.
3. An itemised breakdown of labour and materials for each item, including the floorboard and carpet and the new Venetian blind, and whether VAT applies.
4. Why the floorboard and lounge blind were replaced rather than repaired.

The invoice is on hold until we have reviewed these details. Please reply by email.

Kind regards,
Donna
Northbridge Lettings

input.subject: 18 Brindle Row – ref R/019 – remedial works invoice on hold
input.body:
Dear Mr Marlow,

I'm writing with an update on the move-out remedial works at 18 Brindle Row, Larkspur Vale, ZZ1 1ZZ (ref R/019).

We asked Alder & Finch Repairs for a quotation only. They have now told us they carried out the works and have sent an invoice for £174.00 (one lump sum, not itemised). We had not agreed a price or issued written authority, and we have not yet verified the work. The invoice includes replacing a floorboard and supplying a new Venetian blind, which goes beyond the repairs originally described.

We are holding the invoice and have asked the contractor for photos, the date of their visit, how they got in and an itemised breakdown. A member of our team will also check the property and contact you before anything is paid. You don't need to do anything at the moment, and we'll update you once we have the contractor's reply.

Kind regards,
Donna
Northbridge Lettings

It also includes replacements that weren't authorised: a floorboard plus carpet reinstatement, and a new Venetian blind. The property is vacant and the agency held the keys, so how he got in is a security question. The rules say an invoice that doesn't match an approved quote gets escalated, not paid. Jev also flagged the invoice for review (needs a human response: 0.84).

The landlord did approve the works in general, so whether to accept the invoice is a decision for agency staff and the landlord.
